facts.statement: The genus Panphagia was described in 2009.
facts.quote: Panphagia is a genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur described in 2009.

facts.statement: Fossils of Panphagia were found in the La Peña Member of the Ischigualasto Formation within the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin.
facts.quote: Fossils of the genus were found in the La Peña Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin.

facts.statement: Ricardo N. Martínez discovered Panphagia fossils in late 2006 in the Ischigualasto Formation of San Juan Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Fossils of Panphagia were found in late 2006 by the Argentinean paleontologist Ricardo N. Martínez in rocks of the Ischigualasto Formation of Valle Pintado, Ischigualasto Provincial Park, San Juan Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Panphagia lived during the early Carnian of the Late Triassic, evidenced by its association with a 231.4 million-year-old ash layer.
facts.quote: The bones were found at approximately the same level as a 231.4 million year old ash layer, indicating it lived during the early Carnian of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: The known remains of Panphagia consist of disarticulated fossils from a single partially grown individual approximately 1.30 meters long.
facts.quote: Panphagia is currently known from holotype PVSJ 874, the disarticulated remains of one partially grown individual of about 1.30 m long.

facts.statement: Panphagia fossils were russet-colored, embedded in greenish sandstone, and required several years to prepare and describe.
facts.quote: The russet-colored fossils were embedded in a greenish sandstone matrix and took several years to prepare and describe.

facts.statement: Panphagia was described in 2009 by Ricardo N. Martínez and Oscar A. Alcober of the Museo de Ciencias Naturales in San Juan, Argentina.
facts.quote: Panphagia was described in 2009 by Ricardo N. Martínez and Oscar A. Alcober, both of the Museo de Ciencias Naturales, in San Juan, Argentina.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis identified Panphagia as the most basal known sauropodomorph dinosaur.
facts.quote: They performed a phylogenetic analysis and found it to be the most basal known sauropodomorph dinosaur

facts.statement: Panphagia shares skeletal similarities with Saturnalia, including features of the ischium, astragalus, and scapular blade.
facts.quote: the fossils shared similar features to those of Saturnalia, an early sauropodomorph, including similarities in the ischium, astragalus, and the scapular blade.

facts.statement: Panphagia exhibits features similar to Eoraptor, such as hollow bones, sublanceolate teeth, and general body proportions.
facts.quote: Yet the fossils also exhibited similar features to those of Eoraptor, an early omnivorous sauropodomorph, including hollow bones, sublanceolate teeth, and overall proportions.

facts.statement: Panphagia's teeth suggest an omnivorous diet, representing a transitional form between carnivorous theropods and herbivorous sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: The teeth of Panphagia indicate a possible omnivorous diet, transitional in form between the mostly carnivorous theropods and the herbivorous sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: Panphagia's skull resembles that of other basal saurischians like Eoraptor, and its lower jaw is more delicate.
facts.quote: El cráneo es similar al de otros saurisquios basales como Eoraptor, y su mandíbula inferior es más delicada.

facts.statement: Panphagia possessed approximately 23 teeth that varied in shape depending on their position in the jaw.
facts.quote: Los dientes, alrededor de 23, varían de forma según su posición.

facts.statement: Panphagia's front teeth were recurved and sharp for eating meat, while the back teeth were vertical and spatulate, resembling those of herbivores.
facts.quote: Los frontales son más recurvados y afilados, ideales para comer carne. Los posteriores son más verticales y espatulados más parecidos a los de los herbívoros.

facts.statement: The variation in tooth shape supports the theory that Panphagia was omnivorous, evolving from a carnivorous ancestor toward a herbivorous descendant.
facts.quote: Lo que lleva a la teoría de que este dinosaurio era omnívoro, encontrándose en el camino evolutivo de un ancestro carnívoro a un descendiente herbívoro.

facts.statement: According to phylogenetic analysis, Panphagia is considered the oldest and most primitive sauropodomorph, displacing Saturnalia from that position.
facts.quote: Según su análisis filogenético presentado por los autores, Panphagia es considerado el más antiguo y primitivo de Sauropodomopha, desplazando de este sitio al Saturnalia proveniente de la Formación Santa Maria del Brasil descrito en 1999.

facts.statement: Panphagia's presence in ancient strata suggests that the sauropodomorph clade separated from the saurischian common stem early in dinosaur history, possibly starting ten million years earlier in the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: Su presencia en estratos tan antiguos muestra que este clado ya se había separado del tronco común de los saurisquios temprano en la historia de los dinosaurios y que el comienzo de esta podría haber comenzado unos diez millones de años antes en el Triásico Medio.

facts.statement: The time range for Panphagia is estimated between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)
